attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known reduction converts a small residual correction R_A into a small SAT solver or separator on the generated formula range. This is the current formal gap.
steps: Start with the previous approximate relaxed bag-separator lemma: if A is correct on all but E source bags, then sparse equality patching gives C(H_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}+N^q C(A)+O(NE).
Replace the support-size patch by the exact identity H_N=S_A xor R_A, where R_A=H_N xor S_A. This yields the sharper upper bound in L32.1 without assuming the error set is sparse.
Try to derive C(R_A)>N^{1+epsilon} from hardness of SAT on the generated range U_N={G_N(x,j)}.

The derivation fails because R_A is a function of whole source bags x, not a predicate on individual formulas. It can encode global correlations among generated queries and may be small even if every range-restricted SAT predicate is hard.
Thus promise SAT hardness, semantic range entropy, and label balance do not imply the needed source lower bound unless they also rule out low-complexity residual corrections.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid, but proving Phi_N>1+epsilon-o(1) is still a general circuit lower bound for a specially generated function and may require non-natural, nonrelativizing information about G_N.

assumptions: General nonuniform Boolean circuits with fan-in two gates are the source lower-bound model.
M=N^q, L=(log N)^d, d>1, and q,rho are constants independent of SAT circuit exponent c.
The generator cost N^{rho+o(1)} is charged once for producing or multiplexing all queried formulas.
The lower-bound claim under audit is C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
definitions: source object: H_N:{0,1}^N -> {0,1}, H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M} SAT(G_N(x,j)), where M=N^q and G_N outputs L=(log N)^d bit SAT instances.
target object: SAT on L-bit instances, with target consequence SAT notin P/poly when the bridge is combined with q,rho<1+epsilon and d>1.
controlled interface: the whole bag list x -> (G_N(x,1),...,G_N(x,M)) has circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}, and a local predicate A sees only one generated formula.
target-preserving condition: d>1 and max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, so substituting any fixed polynomial-size SAT circuit costs N^{o(1)} and preserves the lower-bound threshold.
S_A(x)=OR_{j<=M} A(G_N(x,j)) is the bag decision induced by the local predicate A.
R_A(x)=H_N(x) xor S_A(x) is the exact correction residual; set log_N C(0)=-infty.

equations.label: carrier
equations.valid_when: Valid when the generated bag interface and SAT encoding are fixed for input length N.

equations.label: separator_residual
equations.valid_when: Valid when A is any nonuniform predicate on one generated L-bit formula.

equations.label: correction_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after composing A with every generated query and xoring the residual correction circuit.

equations.label: necessary_gate
equations.valid_when: Requires the source lower bound to be against the same nonuniform circuit model used by the correction construction.

equations.label: sparse_error_patch
equations.valid_when: Valid when erroneous bags are patched by equality tests on N-bit source inputs.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find A with C(A)<=N^{1+epsilon-q-gamma} and C(R_A)<=N^{1+epsilon-gamma}; this is a valid subthreshold circuit for H_N and kills the carrier route.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Replaces approximate bag-error counting by the exact source-obligation quantity. It gives a concrete falsifier: a small A with a small residual correction collapses the claimed source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Exact correction-residual audit: an N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for a generated-OR carrier is valid only if every small local formula predicate leaves a high-complexity residual correction H_N xor S_A; approximate bad-bag counting is only a sparse-residual corollary.

assumptions: q,rho<1+epsilon.
The SAT circuit family is nonuniform but has no dependence on the N-bit source input except through L(N).
The generated formulas are honest SAT instances, not promise strings outside the target language.
definitions: SAT circuit hypothesis: for some fixed c, SAT on n-bit instances has circuits of size n^c.
Query length: L(N)=(log N)^d with fixed d>1.
Local predicate choice: A is the assumed SAT circuit restricted to length L(N).

equations.label: polylog_substitution
equations.valid_when: Valid for every fixed polynomial SAT exponent c and fixed polylogarithmic query exponent d.

equations.label: zero_residual
equations.valid_when: Requires generated query strings to be exact SAT encodings in the target language.

equations.label: target_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after the generator list cost and all substituted SAT circuits stay below the threshold.

equations.label: magnified_consequence
equations.latex: C(H_N)>N^{1+\epsilon-o(1)}\ \wedge\ \max\{\rho,q\}<1+\epsilon\Rightarrow SAT\notin SIZE(n^c)\text{ for every fixed }c
equations.valid_when: Requires the lower bound to hold for the same carrier family across all sufficiently large N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If rho>=1+epsilon or q>=1+epsilon, the transfer threshold collapses and the lower bound no longer separates SAT from P/poly.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Preserves the route-level bridge from a barely-superlinear carrier lower bound to SAT notin P/poly, while isolating the source lower-bound burden.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Target bridge with zero residual: if SAT has polynomial-size circuits, the same generated-OR carrier has circuits of size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}; hence a valid H_N>N^{1+epsilon} lower bound with max{rho,q}<1+epsilon excludes every fixed SAT circuit exponent.

assumptions: A ranges over all nonuniform predicates on L-bit generated formulas, not only predicates approximating SAT globally.
Residual circuits may use arbitrary nonuniform advice about the N-bit source domain.
The target bridge remains unchanged and does not justify the source lower bound.
definitions: Residual complexity profile: Phi_N=min_A max{rho,q+log_N C(A),log_N C(H_N xor S_A)}.
Structured leakage: R_A may have low circuit complexity even when its support is large.
Barrier note: a counting or density proof of Phi_N lower bounds would be natural-proof-like unless it is generator-specific and non-large.

equations.label: profile_definition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the minimization ranges over all local formula predicates of length L(N).

equations.label: profile_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when logarithmic exponents are interpreted with the fixed N-parameterized circuit measure.

equations.label: profile_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Requires gamma to be a fixed positive margin over the hidden subpolynomial factors.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A low-complexity residual, even with large support, is a falsifier for any lower-bound proof that only certifies many bad bags.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns nonuniform leakage into a single minimization target that a source lower-bound proof must defeat.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Structured residual leakage is stronger than sparse-error leakage: many wrong bags can still be harmless if H_N xor S_A has a small circuit, so source audits must lower-bound residual complexity rather than error cardinality.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a broad class of generated-OR carriers admits low-complexity residuals from simple local predicates, making Phi_N subthreshold by construction.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if we can prove a non-natural, generator-specific lower bound Phi_N>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} while keeping q,rho<1+epsilon and d>1.
control_decision.reason: This is a contribution-making repair: it gives a precise source-model obstruction and a quantitative transfer/falsifier, rather than repeating hardness magnification folklore.

dependency_updates.description: Approximate bad-bag counting is replaced by the exact minimization over local predicates and correction residuals Phi_N.
The target-preserving transfer remains SAT in SIZE(n^c) => C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} for d>1.
Leakage may occur through a residual circuit on source bags, not only through selected-image SAT solvers or sparse exceptional bags.
A future Phi_N lower bound must avoid being merely a large constructive property of H_N truth tables; otherwise it is natural-proof-like under PRF assumptions.

falsifiers: correction-residual falsifier: exists A with q+log_N C(A)<1+epsilon and C(H_N xor S_A)<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
structured-error falsifier: the bad-bag set is large but has a simple residual circuit, so counting errors would falsely suggest hardness.
threshold-collapse falsifier: q>=1+epsilon or rho>=1+epsilon makes the target transfer too expensive.
nonuniform-leakage falsifier: residual advice about source bags repairs an imperfect local separator without yielding any SAT solver.

natural-proof obstruction: a large constructive property separating H_N from N^{1+epsilon} circuits would conflict with standard pseudorandom-function barriers unless the proof is carrier-specific and non-large.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: If some t gives q+log_N C(A_t)<1+epsilon and r_t<1+epsilon, then the carrier has a concrete subthreshold circuit despite possibly high semantic range entropy. If all simple A_t leave residuals above threshold, the source audit survives this leakage test.
held_fixed_controls: q,rho<1+epsilon so the target transfer remains valid.
d>1 so exhaustive truth-table lookup is not a subthreshold explanation.
The generated strings remain honest SAT encodings of length L(N).
A_t is local to one formula and receives no direct source input x.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Use now as a falsifier probe for generated-OR carrier proposals.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route no longer fails only through sparse bad bags; it fails whenever an imperfect local predicate has a low-complexity residual correction. A concrete experiment tests whether candidate generators accidentally expose such residual structure.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Take H_N(x)=OR_{j<=N^q} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with L=(log N)^d, d>1. Plant or audit a local predicate A_t on generated formulas, then compute or upper-bound R_t(x)=H_N(x) xor OR_j A_t(G_N(x,j)) for a family of tagged or low-rank bag generators.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before the intuition affects proof obligations, exhibit explicit circuits for A_t and R_t or prove lower bounds for every such residual; also certify that the generator cost, query length, and SAT-language honesty are preserved.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: residual circuit exponent r_t=log_N C(R_t), including the sparse case r_t=1+delta when R_t has N^delta exceptional bags.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 32 converts the approximate bag-separator gate into an exact correction-residual gate. The valid target bridge is unchanged, but the source lower bound must prove Phi_N>1+epsilon-o(1): every small local formula predicate must leave a residual H_N xor S_A of high circuit complexity. Sparse error patching is only one falsifier; structured residual leakage is the stronger obstruction.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate Phi_N for a tagged generated-OR carrier and compute whether simple tag predicates produce subthreshold residual circuits; then test an untagged high-entropy generator for the same residual leakage.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Discrepancy lower bounds measure communication under one partition; full circuit size can be small while discrepancy is low. The missing bridge is false for SIZE(poly).
steps: Encode SAT on 2r-bit instances as a matrix M_SAT under a fixed balanced split.
Assume a proposed method proves Disc_U(M_SAT)<=N^{-1/4}.
Try to define R={f: Disc_U(M_f)<=N^{-1/4}} as the separator property for SIZE((2r)^k).
Use the random-matrix calculation to note that R is large at this threshold.
Use IP_r as a substitution test for usefulness: IP_r lies in R but has O(r)-size circuits.
Conclude that the transfer to full circuit lower bounds is invalid unless the method proves an additional theorem excluding all small circuits from low discrepancy, which IP makes impossible.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This certifies a route failure and a restricted repair, but it gives no lower bound for SAT and no evidence for P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: discrepancy carrier audit

assumptions: Discrepancy is rectangle discrepancy under the uniform distribution on [2^r] x [2^r].
IP_r(x,y)=<x,y> mod 2 is encoded as a 2^r x 2^r Hadamard sign matrix.
The target is full nonuniform circuit size, not formula size, monotone circuits, AC0, or low-communication circuits.
A valid route-level transfer must prove usefulness against the named target class before natural-proof or relativization escape claims matter.
definitions: source object: a sign matrix M_f in {+1,-1}^{2^r x 2^r} obtained from a Boolean truth table f:{0,1}^{2r}-> {0,1} under the fixed split x|y.
target object: nonuniform Boolean circuits SIZE((2r)^k) for the original 2r-bit function, with fixed k>=1.
controlled interface: a proposed separator property R_{r,delta} accepts f when Disc_U(M_f)<=delta, and it may transfer only if every function in the target circuit class is rejected.
target-preserving condition: the matrix measure must exclude all SIZE((2r)^k) functions under the same encoding, not merely exclude low-cost communication protocols for the chosen partition.

equations.label: matrix_length
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source object is a balanced two-party split of a 2r-bit truth table.

equations.label: ip_discrepancy
equations.valid_when: Valid when discrepancy is measured uniformly over rectangles and IP gives a Hadamard matrix.

equations.label: ip_circuit_size
equations.valid_when: Valid when the target class is ordinary Boolean circuits over the 2r input bits.

equations.label: random_largeness_scale
equations.valid_when: Valid when a union bound ranges over all rectangles in an n by n random sign matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A claimed SAT-to-circuit lower-bound transfer from Disc_U(M_SAT)<=N^{-1/4} is falsified by substituting IP_r, which satisfies the discrepancy conclusion while remaining in SIZE(O(r)).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a refutation lemma for discrepancy-as-full-circuit carriers: the property is large at the random scale and accepts an easy function, hence it is not useful for SIZE(poly).
candidate_lemmas.statement: Uniform two-party discrepancy of a balanced truth-table matrix is not a target-preserving carrier for full polynomial-size circuit lower bounds. The inner-product matrix has optimal low discrepancy but is computed by linear-size circuits, so any route using only low discrepancy must either restrict the target to low-communication models or add a new bridge not implied by discrepancy.

assumptions: A c-bit deterministic protocol partitions the matrix into at most 2^c monochromatic rectangles.
Uniform discrepancy is the maximum normalized imbalance over rectangles.
For unrestricted circuits of size s, the generic communication simulation has cost O(s log s), which can make the required discrepancy threshold exponentially too small.
definitions: source object: the same split truth-table matrix M_f for f:{0,1}^{2r}-> {0,1}.
target object: a restricted class C_r such that each g in C_r has a deterministic x|y communication protocol using at most c(r) bits.
controlled interface: replace circuit usefulness by protocol usefulness, with the same input partition and uniform rectangle measure.
target-preserving condition: every circuit model claimed as a target must be accompanied by a proved simulation into c(r)-bit protocols under the fixed split.

equations.label: protocol_discrepancy_floor
equations.valid_when: Applies when the protocol is deterministic and computes the whole matrix without promise errors.

equations.label: valid_restricted_separation
equations.valid_when: Requires every member of the restricted target C_r to have a c(r)-bit protocol under this split.

equations.label: full_circuit_threshold_collapse
equations.valid_when: Valid when only the standard gate-by-gate communication simulation of arbitrary circuits is available.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the intended target is full SIZE((2r)^k), the required threshold falls far below the N^{-1/4} random/IP scale and no longer supports the advertised transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This repairs the route by preserving a valid consequence: discrepancy lower bounds transfer to communication-limited targets, not to P versus NP targets.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Low discrepancy gives a valid lower bound only for targets whose members have deterministic communication protocols of cost c under the same split. If Disc_U(M_f)<2^{-c}, then f has deterministic communication complexity greater than c; this does not imply a full circuit lower bound unless a separate circuit-to-protocol upper bound with small c is target-preserving.

control_decision.pivot_test: If the next proposal still targets full SIZE(poly) using only rectangle discrepancy or communication complexity under one split, reject it by the IP falsifier.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the target is renamed to a class with proved c(r)-bit protocols, or if a new source object avoids all known easy low-discrepancy functions without leaking the target.
control_decision.reason: The route fails for P vs NP because its source measure does not reject all small circuits; IP_r is an explicit valid counterexample. A restricted communication-complexity consequence remains mathematically valid.

dependency_updates.description: Low discrepancy at the random scale is large, but the property fails usefulness against SIZE(poly). If a poly(N)-constructive useful variant were proposed for another target, it would then face the usual natural-proof/PRF audit.

The discrepancy argument is a black-box truth-table/matrix argument and does not use nonrelativizing SAT syntax. It cannot be promoted as a P-vs-NP route without a nonrelativizing target-preserving bridge.
No algebraic extension feature is doing work here; the decisive obstruction is usefulness collapse caused by easy low-discrepancy functions.
For restricted classes with c(r)-bit protocols, Disc<2^{-c(r)} gives a valid lower-bound transfer. The branch should track this separately from full circuit lower bounds.

falsifiers: IP_r is a concrete falsifier for usefulness of low-discrepancy properties against full polynomial-size circuits.
A route that only proves high communication complexity or low discrepancy under one split is invalid for P vs NP unless it names a target-preserving circuit-to-protocol bridge.
The threshold delta=N^{-1/4} is compatible with random largeness and with an easy O(r)-circuit function, so largeness alone is not the obstruction.
Exact discrepancy may also lose poly(N) constructivity; however the stronger failure here is lack of usefulness even before constructivity is audited.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For alpha<=1/4, IP_r is accepted by the low-discrepancy property while remaining easy for circuits; for alpha>1/4, the route must show SAT has much smaller-than-Hadamard discrepancy and still must explain why all small circuits have larger discrepancy, which IP refutes at the full-circuit level.
held_fixed_controls: The target class is full nonuniform SIZE((2r)^k), not a communication class.
The split x|y and uniform rectangle discrepancy definition are fixed.
No advice or promise is allowed to remove IP_r from the target class.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Use now as a falsifier probe and restricted-transfer calibration.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs a concrete target-preserving test because discrepancy looks like a strong lower-bound certificate but may silently change the target from circuits to protocols.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Compare two matrices under the same x|y split: M_SAT for padded SAT instances of length 2r and M_IP for inner product on r+r bits, while the target remains SIZE((2r)^k).
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A valid certificate would be either a restriction of the target to c-bit protocol classes with Disc<2^{-c}, or a new nonblack-box theorem relating full circuit size to discrepancy; the latter is impossible in this form because IP_r is an explicit counterexample.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The discrepancy threshold delta=N^{-alpha}, varying alpha around 1/4 and around the protocol threshold c(r)=alpha log N.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 32 separates communication-matrix hardness from circuit hardness. Low uniform discrepancy is dense and can certify lower bounds for low-communication targets, but IP_r is a small-circuit low-discrepancy falsifier for full SIZE(poly). The valid contribution is a target-preservation gate: discrepancy routes must state the circuit-to-protocol threshold c(r), and for arbitrary circuits that threshold collapses to 2^{-Theta(r^k log r)} rather than the random N^{-1/4} scale.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit whether discrepancy of SAT under formula-variable splits yields any nontrivial lower bound for a named restricted class such as small-depth circuits with low cross-partition communication, and compute the exact c(r) threshold before considering any broader circuit claim.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation still assumes a source theorem producing a bounded-D, cap-compatible, no-advice image family with at least one 2^{epsilon m}-hard image; no such theorem is constructed here.
steps: Let I_m be the canonical set of distinct accepted images with log |I_m| <= Dm+o(m); rank each image by j of length Dm+o(m).
Define L_V(j,x,p)=f_j(x), ignoring padding p. Sequential canonical unranking emits f_j and returns the x-th bit in time 2^{O(m)}, so L_V is in E on input length n=(1+D)m+o(m).

Assume L_V has circuits of size 2^{delta n} on the padded target lengths. Hardwire the rank j* of a source-hard image f_{j*} and the padding convention to obtain circuits for f_{j*} of size 2^{delta(1+D)m+o(m)}.
With kappa-dense padding, the exponent becomes delta kappa(1+D). If delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)), this contradicts C(f_{j*})>2^{epsilon m}.

Now audit leakage: if the same source gives bit access f_j(x) in time 2^{beta m+o(m)}, standard circuit simulation gives C(f_j)<=2^{beta m+o(m)}. Thus beta<epsilon contradicts the no-side source claim before extraction begins.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route-level bridge and falsifier audit, not P != NP. The hard source theorem is essentially an E lower-bound-bearing object unless obtained by a genuinely non-natural, nonuniform-free argument.

assumptions: For infinitely many or all kappa-dense source lengths m, some f in I_m has circuit complexity C(f)>2^{epsilon m}.
The number of distinct canonical images satisfies |I_m| <= 2^{D m+o(m)} for a constant D.
Canonical unranking and evaluation of L_V run in 2^{O(m)} time uniformly, possibly by sequentially emitting the whole table.
The padding map from source length m to target input length n preserves uniformity and has gap at most kappa.
If a proposed source supplies bit access in time 2^{beta m+o(m)}, then beta is declared and audited against epsilon.
definitions: source object: a uniform certificate verifier V_m with O(m)-bit certificates whose accepted transcripts emit truth tables f:{0,1}^m -> {0,1}; I_m is the set of distinct emitted tables after an E-canonical quotient.
target object: the multiplexed E language L_V on inputs (j,x,pad), where j is the canonical rank of an image in I_m and L_V(j,x)=f_j(x).

controlled interface: E-canonical distinct-image unranking may be sequential and full-table; a separate bit decoder with time 2^{beta m+o(m)} is treated as leakage, not as part of the bridge requirement.

target-preserving condition: source lengths are kappa-dense, image entropy is D, at least one canonical image at each source length has MCSP complexity above 2^{epsilon m}, epsilon is below the verifier cap alpha_V, and no advice or nonuniform length selector is used.

equations.label: image_entropy
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source carrier has an E-canonical quotient and distinct images are counted at each source length.

equations.label: source_no_side
equations.valid_when: Valid when the MCSP no-side claim is existential over the canonical image family and uses the same truth-table length m.

equations.label: multiplexed_length
equations.valid_when: Valid when canonical ranks use Dm+o(m) bits and the queried truth-table input contributes m bits.

equations.label: target_lower_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after the reduction preserves uniformity, kappa-density, canonical ranking, and the MCSP threshold parameter epsilon.

equations.label: random_access_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Requires a uniform bit decoder for every canonical image whose running time can be circuitized with only polynomial overhead.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If canonical unranking is nonuniform, if D is unbounded, if kappa is unbounded, or if a decoder with beta<epsilon exists, the carrier cannot validly support the claimed E lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates valid extraction from invalid source leakage: bounded image entropy gives the multiplexing loss, while subthreshold bit access destroys the claimed MCSP hardness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Access-profile bridge for bounded-image MCSP carriers: a uniform low-distinct-image MCSP no-side carrier transfers to an E lower bound with exponent loss kappa(1+D), while any subthreshold random-access decoder for the same images is a formal source falsifier.

assumptions: Circuitizing a sequential scan gives size about 2^{m+o(m)} on m input bits.
The intended MCSP threshold exponent epsilon is a fixed constant less than one.
No hidden checkpoint mechanism stores 2^{o(m)}-size summaries allowing subthreshold random access.
definitions: A sequential emitter outputs f(0^m),...,f(1^m-1) in lexicographic order and may require scanning from the beginning to answer one bit.
A bit decoder answers f(x) directly from (m,j,x) without emitting the preceding table prefix.
The source claim is audited against the best declared or derivable indexed access, not against mere existence of an E-time sequential computation.

equations.label: sequential_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the only available uniform evaluation method scans a length 2^m table sequentially from the start.

equations.label: compatibility_window
equations.valid_when: Applies when the source threshold is below full truth-table scan cost and no faster decoder is supplied.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma fails if the verifier transcript includes restartable checkpoints, low-locality blocks, or a random-access circuit family below exponent epsilon.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents over-quarantining the route: E-canonical sequential explicitness is enough for the target language but does not automatically refute subexponential MCSP hardness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Sequential full-table generation in time 2^{m+o(m)} is not by itself a falsifier for an MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m} with epsilon<1; only faster indexed access or checkpoint replay below the threshold yields small circuits for the emitted table.

assumptions: D is constant and |I_m|<=2^{Dm+o(m)}.
Circuits of size s=2^{epsilon m} have descriptions of length O(s log s).
The carrier image is sparse rather than dense in all 2^{2^m} truth tables.
definitions: The low-complexity set at length m consists of truth tables computed by circuits of size at most 2^{epsilon m}.
A counting-only source proof would compare |I_m| with the complement of the low-complexity set without using non-natural structure.
The obstruction is quantitative and does not refute non-counting, non-natural certificates.

equations.label: small_circuit_count
equations.valid_when: Valid when Boolean circuits use a standard finite encoding with O(s log s) description length.

equations.label: counting_gap
equations.valid_when: Valid for every fixed positive epsilon and constant D as the truth-table input length m tends to infinity.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed proof says a sparse image family must contain a hard function merely by counting, this inequality is the falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Rules out a tempting but invalid source construction method and forces the source theorem to use a structural, non-natural, non-enumerative argument.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A bounded-D image family cannot obtain a constant epsilon MCSP no-side theorem from counting alone; the number of small circuits is exponentially larger than the image family for every constant epsilon>0.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if every candidate source either uses beta<epsilon random access, nonuniform hard-rank advice, unbounded D, or a counting-only argument.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving a constant-epsilon bounded-D source theorem with declared verifier cap alpha_V>=epsilon and no subthreshold indexed decoder.
control_decision.reason: The route gained a concrete falsifier and preserved a valid extraction theorem, but the bounded-D MCSP source theorem remains the decisive missing object.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier must now declare an access profile: sequential E-canonical generation is acceptable, but any indexed access below the MCSP exponent is a falsifier.
The valid exponent transfer remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)); certificate count is irrelevant once distinct-image ranking is canonical.
Explicitness means uniform E evaluation of the multiplexed language, not necessarily low-time random access to each source image.
Need a bounded-D, cap-compatible, non-natural proof that some canonical image has MCSP complexity above 2^{epsilon m}. Counting cannot provide it.

falsifiers: Subthreshold bit-access falsifier: a decoder for canonical images running in 2^{beta m+o(m)} time with beta<epsilon gives small circuits for every emitted table.
Entropy-collapse falsifier: D_m growing with m makes delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D_m)) vanish.
Gap-collapse falsifier: nonconstant kappa in the source-length schedule removes any fixed E lower-bound exponent.
Advice falsifier: choosing the hard canonical rank j_m nonuniformly without multiplexing or uniform ranking invalidates the target object.
Cap falsifier: epsilon>alpha_V exceeds the verifier checkpoint/profile upper bound and makes the MCSP source unsound.
Naturalness falsifier: adding dense random salt to make the image large restores constructivity plus largeness and falls into the natural-proofs obstruction.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For beta<0.4 the source is refuted because each image has circuits below the claimed threshold; for beta>=0.4 sequential evaluation remains compatible and the extracted lower-bound exponent can approach 0.4/1.1.
held_fixed_controls: No advice in the rank selection or source-length schedule.
Linear certificates and E-canonical distinct-image unranking remain available.
The target language is the same multiplexed E language L_V.
